correctness.rationale: Fresh symbolic differentiation gives \(\dot Q=2zQ\) and, with \(u=w-1\), \(\dot u=zu\), hence \(u/\sqrt Q\) is constant. A compact invariant support cannot meet \(Q=0\): there \(x=y=0\) and \(\dot z=1\). Thus \(\log Q\) is smooth on the support and invariance gives \(\int z\,d\mu=0\). The pure fourth-coordinate variational line is invariant with exponent zero; the quotient is the 3D base with divergence \(2z\), exponent sum zero, and a zero autonomous-flow exponent because there is no equilibrium on compact support. Its remaining exponents are opposite, giving the full spectrum.
correctness.risk: The statement is asymptotic and measure-theoretic on compact invariant supports; it does not diagnose a specific finite-time Lyapunov algorithm.

final_claim: For the Liu--Du--Zhang--Li--Shi four-dimensional flow with \(a,b>0\), \(Q=bx^2+ay^2\) satisfies \(\dot Q=2zQ\), so \((w-1)^2/Q\) is a first integral on \(Q>0\). Every compact ergodic invariant probability measure lies in that region, has \(\int z\,d\mu=0\), and has Lyapunov spectrum \(\{\lambda,0,0,-\lambda\}\), hence at most one positive asymptotic exponent.
limitations: Only compact ergodic invariant probability measures and asymptotic Oseledets exponents are covered.
